Subject: Retention & backup purge timelines — DPA addendum + subprocessor evidence

Paul —

Following our call this morning, I wanted to capture the ask in writing so Legal and Ops have the same source of truth. Two items we need to align on before finalizing the DPA addendum:

1) Backup purge timeline (cross-border staging): when we run our cross-border export for processing in the US, what maximum staging window can Medscope accept before datasets are returned to EU-resident storage? We proposed a 14-day staging window during our call.
2) Audit/log retention exceptions: you mentioned a 90-day SLA for audit logs used for diagnosis and regulatory audits — please confirm whether that applies to forensic logs only or all request/response telemetry.

Attached: Medscope_DPA_v2.docx (draft addendum), redwood_backup_schedule_v3.xlsx (proposed purge windows).

If those two points are acceptable we can:
- add the cross-border staging carveout to section 4.2 of the DPA
- require a signed subprocessor attestation for any new vendor taking custody of backups during the staging window

Can you confirm by end of week? If helpful I can loop in Marissa (Security Ops) and Karthik (Legal) to finalize language.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Retention & backup purge timelines — DPA addendum + subprocessor evidence

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers:

• Staging window: 14 days is acceptable as a maximum for staging in the US, provided Medscope receives written evidence that any US subprocessor holds data only transiently and that EU-resident copies are the canonical copies.

• Logs: the 90-day retention we're comfortable with applies to operational/diagnostic logs (error traces, server-side request logs) required for incident investigation. We cannot accept 90 days for user-level message content or analytic event streams that contain PII unless encrypted and access-controlled; for those we prefer a 30-day max unless there's a documented legal hold.

We can provide a redacted SOC or compliance summary for initial review. I'll ask Legal Ops to pull our standard attestation template; attaching their note now.

Paul Heath
General Counsel, Medscope Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention & backup purge timelines — DPA addendum + subprocessor evidence

Paul —

Appreciate the quick reply and the attestation sample. I've sketched an operational timeline and a minimal evidence checklist below so Legal can sign off quickly: 

Operational proposal (Redwood):
- Cross-border staging: up to 14 days in US-resident encrypted staging buckets (AES-256).
- Automatic sync back to EU-resident storage on day 14; if restore is needed during staging, we auto-replicate the returned dataset to EU storage within 48 hours after the restore completes.
- Backups (canonical copies): retained in-region (EU) unless customer-authorized staging is used.

Log classification and retention (Redwood):
- Forensic/operational logs (error traces, kernel-level traces): 90 days (access controlled to Security/Support).
- Request/response telemetry containing customer PII: 30 days default; can be reduced per customer request.
- Immutable audit trail (high-level): 365 days for compliance metadata (no PII).

Minimum evidence checklist for subprocessor access during staging:
- Signed attestation from the subprocessor confirming transient custody and encryption policy.
- Confirmation of access controls (role separation + KMS usage).
- Completed Data Transfer Impact Assessment (DTIA) if EU→US cross-border transfer.

If Medscope is OK with the proposal above we will:
1) Add a short carveout clause to section 4.2 of the DPA (staging window + attestation requirement).
2) Add a definition for "forensic logs" and a retention table in the schedule.

Can Karthik or Irene confirm whether those items are sufficient for Legal? If yes, we'll prepare the DocuSign package and include the attestation template for subprocessors.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_backup_schedule_v3.xlsx (xlsx), subprocessor_attestation_sample.pdf (pdf)]

Marissa / Irene —

That wording looks workable to us with two caveats: 

1) SOC 2 Type II report: we will need a current SOC 2 Type II report (or equivalent) covering the environments that will host EU customer data while in staging. Redacted copies are fine.
2) DocuSign: please include the limited staging carveout and attestation commitment in the electronic signature package. We'll sign once Legal Ops has received the SOC report.

I kicked off an internal ticket for Legal Ops to pull the report and I'll have an update by Thursday. Once we have the SOC report we can countersign the addendum and provide the standard subprocessor attestation for our internal vendors.

Paul Heath
General Counsel, Medscope Health
